summary: Henry County fire tower on Chestnut Knob: CCC steel tower of 1939 (52 ft) and a 100-ft tower dated 1964 by the register; since replaced by communication towers.

facts.status_note: The register says the tower has been replaced by communication towers.

access.note: The register lists the administrator as a private owner; no source we read says whether visitors may reach the summit.

events.note: CCC Company 2345 built a steel tower, 52 feet high, per a November 1939 report quoted on the Forest Lookouts page
Tower manned during fire season, per the 1939 report
Martinsville Bulletin visit describes a 53-foot steel tower with a glass-enclosed watch room
Register date for a 100-foot steel tower; not reconciled with the 1939 tower
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register on March 24, 2020

evidence.supports: 1939 date of the CCC report on Chestnut Knob
source of the 1939 report is Co. 2345 of the CCC
Co. 2345 constructed a steel fire tower on Chestnut Knob, the highest elevation in Henry County
evidence.quote: Co. 2345 recently constructed a steel fire tower on Chestnut Knob, the highest elevation in Henry County.

evidence.supports: tower 52 feet high with an observation room eight feet square
evidence.quote: The tower is fifty-two feet high and has an observation room eight feet square perched on top.

evidence.supports: nearly three miles of telephone line connected the tower to the main line
evidence.quote: Nearly three miles of telephone lines were built to connect the tower with the main line.

evidence.supports: 1939 report says the tower was staffed during fire season
evidence.quote: During the fire season the tower is manned to protect the forests of the county.

evidence.supports: 1961 article describes a 53-foot steel tower on the highest point in central Henry County
evidence.quote: The steel tower at Chestnut Knob is 53 feet high and is built on the highest point in central Henry County.
One can see in all directions from the glass enclosed, rectangular watch tower.

evidence.supports: view of Martinsville to the north
evidence.quote: You can pick out many landmarks of Martinsville proper to the north

evidence.supports: the 1961 article is credited to the Martinsville Bulletin
register dates a 100-foot steel tower to 1964
evidence.quote: This 100-foot steel tower was built in 1964.

evidence.supports: tower has been replaced by communication towers
evidence.quote: It has been replaced by communication towers.

corrections.proposed: 1939 built (CCC steel tower, 52 ft); 1964 kept as the register's date for a 100-ft tower
corrections.why: The Forest Lookouts page quotes a 1939 CCC report of a tower on the summit, and a 1961 Martinsville Bulletin visit describes a 53-foot tower there, both before 1964.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 1964 for a 100-foot steel tower; the Forest Lookouts page gives 1939 for a 52-foot tower and 1961 for a 53-foot tower. No source says whether the 1964 tower replaced the earlier one, so the story gives both sets of figures and does not choose between them.

notes_for_editor: Two sources. The register's 1964 build and 100-foot height do not match the 1939 and 1961 descriptions on the Forest Lookouts page, and neither source explains the difference. A Facebook post found in search repeats the 1939 CCC attribution but was not used. Staffing evidence is the 1939 report only. The 1961 article is quoted through the Forest Lookouts page, not read at the newspaper. No source describes the site today beyond the communication towers.
